summary: Brightline Financial requested a focused review of Redwood's SSO (SAML) and SCIM provisioning flow plus RBAC recommendations. Discussed IdP compatibility, SP-initiated vs IdP-initiated flows, SCIM attribute mapping for groups and custom attributes, audit log retention, KMS/encryption at rest, and data residency. Agreed on next steps: share integration docs, RBAC role mapping spreadsheet, provide test accounts, and schedule a hands-on integration test on 2027-01-07.
topics: SAML SSO setup (SP vs IdP initiated, metadata exchange)
SCIM provisioning and group sync (attributes, filtering)
Encryption, KMS, and data residency concerns
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-27
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Lena O, Caleb N, Priya S (Redwood) — Marcus R, Elaine P, Jonah L (Brightline)

[00:00] Lena Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, then we'll jump into the SSO/SCIM and RBAC review. Marcus?
[00:07] Marcus Reed: Hey, Marcus here — CISO. Elaine and Jonah are on as well. Thanks for doing this on short notice.
[00:12] Elaine Park: Elaine, Head of Platform. We're particularly worried about provisioning and least-privilege access.
[00:17] Jonah Lee: Jonah, IAM. I'll be testing the SCIM/roles.
[00:21] Lena Ortiz: Awesome. Caleb is our SE, he'll drive the technical details; Priya will cover security policies.
[00:26] Caleb Nguyen: Hi all, great to meet you. I'll share my screen in a bit — but first, high level: we'll run through SAML metadata exchange, SP vs IdP initiation, then SCIM mapping, group sync, and finally RBAC role mappings and audit logs.

[02:02] Caleb Nguyen: So Brightline, can you describe your IdP? I know from the form you use Okta, correct?
[02:08] Jonah Lee: Yes, Okta for us right now; we have a dev org and prod org, and we prefer IdP-initiated flows for most app launches but can do SP-initiated for certain service accounts.
[02:20] Caleb Nguyen: Okta is straightforward. Redwood supports both SP and IdP-initiated SAML. We provide a metadata XML and an ACS (assertion consumer service) URL. For SP-initiated we also publish an entity ID.
[02:35] Jonah Lee: Great. Question — do you support signed assertions and response/encryption? We require signed assertions and encrypted nameid for prod.
[02:43] Priya Shah: Yes, we support signed SAML assertions and can accept encrypted assertions. For production setups we recommend signed assertions plus TLS for the metadata endpoint. We can also support attribute statements with custom attributes — e.g., employeeType or dept for RBAC mapping.
[03:03] Marcus Reed: Encryption at the SAML layer is good. On SCIM, what's your provisioning model — one-way push from IdP to Redwood or do you support bi-directional?
[03:13] Caleb Nguyen: Our SCIM endpoint is a standard SCIM 2.0 service; we support push provisioning from the IdP into Redwood. We don't expose users back to the IdP — usually customers don't want that. For groups, we consume group membership and map to internal RBAC groups. We also support incremental sync (delta) and full sync depending on Okta config.
[03:29] Elaine Park: Ok, delta sync is needed — we have large teams. Also, can we filter which groups get provisioned? We don't want every sandbox team to reach production.
[03:39] Caleb Nguyen: Yes, we allow group filters — you can pass a SCIM filter or pre-configure allowed group patterns on our side. We recommend scoping by prefix, e.g., "rbw-prod-*" so only prod groups provision.

[05:00] Jonah Lee: For attribution and audit, does SCIM include who initiated the change? We need to map SCIM changes back to an audit trail and preserve the Okta actor.
[05:10] Priya Shah: Our provisioning logs include the SCIM request payload, timestamp, and the authenticated API client ID used by the IdP. We can also ingest the Okta actor via a custom header if your Okta pipeline supports sending it; otherwise we surface the provisioning account. Logs are retained per your retention policy — default 90 days, with enterprise add-on up to 7 years.
[05:33] Marcus Reed: Retention 90 days for standard is fine for now but we may need 3 years for certain audit requirements — is long-term cold storage available?
[05:42] Priya Shah: Yes, with the compliance add-on we can push logs to your S3 in a region you own or store encrypted logs for long-term retention. We also provide a tamper-evident hash chain for high-assurance audit scenarios.

[07:20] Caleb Nguyen: Back to RBAC — typically our customers model three base roles: Admin, Manager, and User. But we also support custom roles and granular permissions. How does Brightline want to map Okta groups to roles?
[07:33] Elaine Park: Ideally: okta group "brightline-rbw-admins" => Redwood Admin; "brightline-rbw-app" => Developer/User with limited access; and a separate group for read-only auditors. We want least privilege by default.
[07:47] Caleb Nguyen: Sounds good. We recommend a principle: only grant Admin to a small set of users; everything else default to minimal privileges. We'll share a mapping spreadsheet.

[09:12] Jonah Lee: A technical nuance — does Redwood support Just-in-Time role elevation or temporary admin sessions? We try to avoid standing admin privileges.
[09:21] Priya Shah: We have support for temporary elevated sessions via short-lived RBAC tokens. Integrations can call our elevation API which issues a scoped session for a configurable TTL and logs the request. It can also require an approval workflow if you want.
[09:38] Marcus Reed: Approval workflow — is that internal to Redwood or do you integrate with our ticketing/approvals?
[09:45] Caleb Nguyen: We can integrate with common ticketing systems or you can use our built-in simple approval module. Most enterprises integrate with ServiceNow or Jira through a webhook.

[11:10] Elaine Park: On encryption and KMS — where are keys stored? We need to ensure customer-controlled keys for PII in our enterprise plan.
[11:18] Priya Shah: For Private deployments or enterprise Dedicated, you can bring-your-own-KMS (BYOK) via AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or Azure Key Vault. For hosted customers we offer Redwood-managed KMS with HSM-backed keys, or we can integrate your KMS in cross-account role config. All at-rest encryption uses AES-256; we also encrypt KV cache contents and model artifacts.
[11:40] Marcus Reed: Do you support envelope encryption so we can rotate keys without re-encrypting everything?
[11:46] Priya Shah: Yes, envelope encryption supported. We rotate data keys and keep the master key in your KMS when BYOK is enabled.

[13:05] Jonah Lee: Data residency — our policy requires inference logs and inputs to stay in EU region for EU customers. Can we force region-only storage?
[13:14] Caleb Nguyen: Yes, we support region pinning. For enterprise customers we can guarantee data never leaves a specified region and can run private deployments in a VPC in your cloud region.

[15:00] Marcus Reed: SOC 2 / ISO docs — we need the latest reports and scope. Are those ready to share under an NDA?
[15:07] Priya Shah: Yes, we can share our SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 certificates under an NDA. We'll drop those in the shared S3/an internal secure link.

[18:20] Elena (crosstalk): — sorry, question on SCIM attributes — if we push custom attribute "cost_center" can we use that to gate model access?
[18:30] Caleb Nguyen: Yep, you can map arbitrary SCIM attributes to internal policy tags. We expose an attribute-to-claim mapping table to use in the RBAC engine, so you can gate model variants or rate limits based on cost_center.

[21:00] Jonah Lee: A corner-case — what about service accounts? We have machine identities that need programmatic provisioning and longer-lived tokens. How do you recommend handling that?
[21:10] Priya Shah: Service accounts should be created as SCIM users with a service flag; we recommend issuing short-lived keys using our IAM broker or a vault integration. For long-running batch jobs we support rotating tokens and scoped API keys with expiry and automatic rotation.

[24:05] Caleb Nguyen: Demo — I'll share the SCIM mapping UI and the RBAC role builder. (screen-share noises) You'll see we can map Okta groups to roles and set attribute filters. There's also a way to preview which users will be in scope before pushing.

[30:00] Marcus Reed: That preview is helpful. For audit requirements we need immutable logs of role assignments changes. Are those captured?
[30:08] Priya Shah: Yes, role assignment changes are recorded with who, when, and prior role. Those logs are part of the audit package and can be exported to your SIEM (Splunk, Sumo, Datadog) in real-time via our logging connector.

[33:45] Elaine Park: About SCIM rate limits — we sync a lot of groups. If we do a full sync, what's the throttling?
[33:53] Caleb Nguyen: Default rate limit is 120 requests/min per tenant for SCIM. For large customers we bump that or provide an async bulk-import endpoint to avoid throttling. We document the recommended Okta job schedules to avoid hot windows.

[38:20] Jonah Lee: Testing plan — we'd like to run a staging integration, then a small pilot with a subset of prod groups. Proposed dates?
[38:28] Lena Ortiz: How about we target integration test the week of Jan 4th and a pilot Jan 10th-7th? We suggested Jan 7th earlier in next steps; does that still work for you?
[38:38] Jonah Lee: Jan 7th integration test works — will create a test Okta dev org and provide creds to your SE.

[42:00] Marcus Reed: Any known compliance gaps we should be aware of — e.g., memory of full user inputs retained with inference logs? We want to minimize PII in logs.
[42:10] Priya Shah: By default, we store inference metadata and short excerpts for quality monitoring. For regulated customers, we offer PII redaction hooks and can disable storing full input payloads. We also support token-level hashing for reference without raw text.

[46:30] Caleb Nguyen: Quick note on fallback: if SCIM provisioning fails we have idempotent retries and a dead-letter queue. We also surface provisioning failures in the console and via webhook.

[49:00] Elaine Park: Sounds good. On RBAC mapping spreadsheet — can you include default least-privilege templates and a recommended set of permissions for our security/audit teams?
[49:08] Lena Ortiz: Yes, we'll include templates: Admin, Audit-only, Dev, Operator, Read-only. We'll also annotate risky permissions.

[51:15] Marcus Reed: Recap please?
[51:20] Lena Ortiz: Recap: 1) We'll send SAML metadata and SCIM endpoints + integration guide (Lena, due 1/4). 2) Caleb will prepare RBAC role mapping spreadsheet and least-privilege templates (due 1/6). 3) Jonah will provide a test Okta tenant and sample group structure (due 1/5). 4) We'll schedule an integration test on 2027-01-07 (Lena to book). We'll also share SOC2/ISO docs under NDA.
[52:10] Marcus Reed: Good. One last ask — please include an example of the audit log JSON schema so our SIEM team can parse it.
[52:20] Priya Shah: Will include the event schema.
[53:00] Lena Ortiz: Great, thanks all. We'll follow up by email with the artifacts.
[53:06] Jonah Lee: Thanks everyone.
[53:10] (meeting ends)
